The Living Practice

A year of the Amari practice, at home.

Living Practice is a self-guided video library of Amari movement: 53+ references, cues, and setups to use on your own floor, for one year.

What it is

A visual practice you can return to all year.

Each video gives you a clear setup: a position, a cue for attention, and a way to explore the movement on your own. You can begin with Living Practice or use it to extend work you have done with Garrett.

It is a complete standalone offering. In-person work adds direct, hands-on guidance when you want a teacher responding to your body in real time.

What's inside.

A growing visual library of movements and setups from the practice.

Visual cues

Return to a clear movement practice at home.

The videos make it easier to revisit key positions, setups, and attention cues when you are practicing at home. They support your own developing physical judgment—not a generic daily routine.

  • A growing library of movement references from the Amari practice
  • Clear visual reminders of positions, props, and cues
  • A place to return to the work whenever it is useful
  • Available on your phone or laptop between sessions

Who it's for.

Use it as a self-guided practice at home, or as a way to revisit and build on work you have learned in person.

Starting at home

You want a clear movement practice you can use on your own.

Alongside in-person work

You want to keep the exact work you have explored close.

The library gives you a visual cue when you want to return to an element of your practice at home, without guessing what Garrett meant or reaching for a random routine.

A living practice
